newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate approves presdential decrees bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate approves presdential decrees bill.

text.p: Brazil's Senate gave a first approval to a bill, which would change rules governing the use of presidential decrees, a congressional official said.

The upper house approved the bill with 57 votes in favor, six more than the three-fifths majority of 51 the legislation needed as a constitutional amendment. Seven senators voted against and two abstained.
The bill needs a second approval in the upper house before being sent to the Chamber of Deputies where it also needs two three-fifths majorities.
The Senate was due to carry on voting Wednesday on a series of proposed amendments to the bill.
The bill seeks to end a long-running battle between the government and Congress by setting down clear rules for presidential decrees, known as MPs by their Portuguese initials.

Lawmakers have long resented the use of MPs, alleging they undermine the role of Congress. But the government says they are essential to implement important legislation quickly, sidestepping the often lengthy process in Congress.
The Real Plan to curb inflation and reform the economy was introduced in 1994 as an MP, which has since been approved.

The new law would extend the validity of a presidential decree to 90 days from the current 30. But it would allow the government to renew an MP for only one extra period of 90 days. Decrees can now be renewed ad infinitum. The bill also sets down new timetables for Congress to approve or reject decrees.
Over 2,000 decrees from past governments have never been put to a vote in Congress and are renewed regularly. President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has issued about 75 decrees of his own.
